attempted_claim: Let K be an imaginary quadratic field of class number one with O_K^x = {±1} (e.g. Q(sqrt(-2)), Q(sqrt(-7)), Q(sqrt(-11))), let E,E'/Q with End Ebar = End Ebar' = O_K, and let Y = Kum(E x E') be the minimal desingularisation of (E x E')/±1. Assume Y has good reduction at a prime p (allowing p=2) with supersingular K3 reduction Y_p/F_q. Determine the 2-primary transcendental group (Br(Y)/Br_1(Y)){2} by completing the Skorobogatov–Zarhin homomorphism description with flat/crystalline methods, and for each 2-power class A decide whether the p-adic evaluation ev_{A,p}: Y(Q_p) -> Br(Q_p) is constant. In particular: does there exist a 2-primary transcendental A with non-constant (hence weak-approximation-obstructing) evaluation when Br_1(Y) = Br(Q), and how does the answer depend on the height/Artin invariant of Y_p?
decisive_failure: The p=2 wild-reduction flat/crystalline evaluation analysis, formal Brauer height computation, and Artin-invariant determination were not performed; external model verification was blocked and only a basic python stack was available, so the core per-class constancy question at 2 remains open and no substitute claim is made.
